content:
Apple has cited a recently paused securities fraud lawsuit to support its request to halt further lower court proceedings in its legal battle with Epic Games while portions of the dispute are considered by the Supreme Court. Details below.

Apple pointed out that Judge Rogers could reference the relevant ruling when considering the request to pause.

Earlier this year, a class action lawsuit was filed on behalf of the City of Coral Springs Police Officers' Pension Plan, alleging that Apple had engaged in securities fraud.

The lawsuit claims Apple misled investors in two areas: first, whether the company was truly complying with the injunction in the Epic Games case, and second, whether it would release its advertised AI-powered Siri features on schedule.

Meanwhile, Apple is continuing to challenge the contempt of court ruling in the Epic case. The Supreme Court is currently examining one question: the 2021 injunction requiring Apple to allow external purchasing options did not explicitly prohibit collecting commissions on consumer spending outside the App Store, and whether Apple can be held in civil contempt for collecting such commissions on these purchases.

Last week, Apple requested the lower court to pause related proceedings to clarify what commissions (if any) the company may collect on consumer spending outside the App Store while the Supreme Court considers the contempt ruling.

Apple argued that the Supreme Court's decision could affect lower court proceedings, though Epic Games disagreed with this argument.

It has been shown that Apple previously filed a similar request to pause in the Coral Springs securities fraud case, as that case also involves the Epic Games case.

Earlier today, Judge Noël Wise granted Apple's request, meaning the Coral Springs case will remain paused until the Supreme Court makes its decision on the civil contempt ruling.

This move prompted Apple to submit Judge Wise's ruling in the Epic Games case to Judge Rogers, arguing that the ruling supports its request to pause the related proceedings.

Excerpt from Apple's petition to Judge Rogers:

Judge Rogers is currently reviewing Apple's arguments in support of staying the case, as well as Epic's arguments against the stay. Apple hopes Judge Wise's ruling will persuade Judge Rogers to reach the same decision.

Notably, in response to Epic's arguments opposing the stay, Apple also requested Judge Gonzalez Rogers that, even if she denies the stay request, she could first temporarily hold the proceedings, giving the company an opportunity to apply to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court to maintain the paused status, while the Supreme Court separately considers the contempt ruling.
